review.rationale: The supplied frozen Gold is a coherent independent expectation for this planning-only C scenario. REQ-001, AC-001–AC-003, DEC-001, task keys, repository identity and base commit agree across the specification, PRD and Gold. C explicitly fixes OPT-1 as a hypothetical benchmark input, without claiming a human Decision; only that selected branch is required. This supports ready with no decision blocker, while an unresolved material DEC-001 in paired B must still block at decisions. The supplied source places normalization, vocabulary sets and truthy-first baseline behavior in core/api.ts, with classic and mini forwarding to that shared factory. The exact writable scope correctly includes that implementation and both regression files; forwarding and declaration consumers remain inspection owners, and the supplied zshy build configuration supports treating emitted declarations as generated rather than separately maintained owners. Acceptance covers construction-time TypeError rejection, normalization and boundary cases without trimming, and preservation of non-overlap, inference and codec behavior. Runtime tests and compiler checks are distinguished and supported by the supplied configuration. TASK-VERIFY is independent and depends on TASK-IMPLEMENT; the specified agents have appropriate roles, availability and active project-scoped trusted claims for the bounded work, including data.change and the verifier-only testing.verification claim. An independent active non-executing Reviewer is configured. Historical project reuse preserves scoped attestations and does not constitute candidate evidence for this bundle. Gold and preview release fingerprints agree; the supplied provenance explains the distinct manifest/evaluation digest domains and PRD trimming. Repository, source, team, decision, prompt, model, sampling, budget and policy fingerprints are supplied as Service-bound inputs. I reviewed their stated consistency without recomputing digests, executing code, creating a human attestation or relying on candidate outputs. Approval concerns the expectation, not task dispatch, implementation correctness or release authorization.
